verdict: This list of sports card grading companies for 2026 starts with AGS and covers PSA, SGC, Beckett, CGC and five more, each with its price, its wait and its catch.

Send the card you will auction to PSA if the premium covers its fee. Send the rest of your sports cards somewhere fast and flat-priced. That is the split most sellers land on, and AGS fits the second job.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

Every slab comes with the evidence. The digital report shows eight subgrades, centering data, high-resolution images and a color-coded heightmap of the surface, red on major flaws and green on clean areas. You can download it or share it by link, and the scan stays on file against the cert number.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

faq.a: AGS, PSA, SGC, Beckett and CGC are the main ones. ISA and GMA are smaller budget options. The list below gives each company's price, wait and main drawback.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.
Yes: basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, including chrome finishes. Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate, or $18, $23 and $33 on the bulk tiers.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.
